newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bear killers get four-year jail terms.
newsitem.headline: Thai bear killers get four-year jail terms.

text.p: A criminal court in Thailand's central Ayudhaya province has sentenced two men to four-year jail terms after finding them guilty of organising commercial bear killing, court officials said on Wednesday.
Veera Sengpanich and Suchart, both Thai nationals, pleaded guilty to the charge of organising the killing of an animal of endangered species.

Police in July arrested four Thais and five South Koreans at a road checkpoint in Ayudhaya, about 100 kms (60 miles) north of capital Bangkok, after they found paws and other parts of six bears hidden in their truck.
The nine suspects confessed that had bought bears at the Thai-Burmese border to supply their paws and meat to Bangkok restaurants that cater mostly to Korean clients.
The Ayudhaya court had in August fined the five South Koreans and three of the four Thais 20,000 baht ($800) each after giving them two-year suspended jail terms.
During their trial, the convicted Koreans and Thais implicated restaurant owner Veera and his colleague Suchart of being behind the bear killing business.
